verdictSummary: The spec itself (e2e/saved-custom-combat-launch.spec.ts, the only change in commit 2d333ee60) is well-constructed, drives the real production route end to end, and its no-substitution proof is sound at 3 of the 4 named points plus a valid identity check at the 4th. Typecheck and oxfmt gates are clean. However my own required live run (axis 5) of the EXACT specified invocation FAILED against the current state of the shared worktree, with a root cause traced to source: the standalone build currently on disk was not built with NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE=true, so src/lib/e2e/storeExposure.ts:31 short-circuits and window.__ZUSTAND_STORES__ is never populated, exactly matching the observed 'Campaign E2E stores are not exposed' failure. This is worktree/build contamination (see gate5 finding below for full chain of evidence), not a defect in the reviewed spec or product code. Per my charter I did not rebuild (the build was present, not missing). The required action before this proof can be certified as verified-live is: rebuild the standalone bundle in an uncontaminated environment with NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE=true NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TEST=true (matching the preparer's original build command), then re-run the exact invocation below and confirm green. No text edit to the spec file is required.

findings.title: Spec drives the real production route end to end
findings.detail: Confirmed by direct read of e2e/saved-custom-combat-launch.spec.ts: custom unit POST /api/units/custom (lines 234-242), combat-catalog admission check (244-246), real create-wizard roster assignment (248-263), server campaign PUT + readback (264-281), Mech Bay resolution (283-285), mission seeded onto the server campaign (287-288), navigation to missions/:id/launch and click of launch-mission-direct (289-301, the exact step every prior spec in this codebase stops short of per the admission brief's existingE2ECoverage survey), navigation to /gameplay/encounters/:id and click of launch-encounter-btn (302-337), pre-battle mode-selection + auto-resolve-btn click (338-364), terminal /gameplay/games/:id game-completed (365-373), post-battle /review + apply-outcome-cta (443-458), and a cold-reloaded /mech-bay + GET /api/campaigns/:id + GET /api/units/custom/:id roster readback (460-476).

findings.title: No-substitution proof: 3 of 4 named points are true armor-VALUE assertions; the 4th ('force record') is an identity-only assertion
findings.detail: Verified against spec lines: (a) in-session GameCreated seed, lines 385-395, asserts seededCustom[0].leftArmArmor === CUSTOM_LEFT_ARM_ARMOR (30), a literal-constant comparison, not against whatever the server returned -- PASS. (b) archived GameCreated snapshot (POST /api/replay-library/encounter body), lines 405-420, asserts archivedCustom[0].armorByLocation.left_arm === CUSTOM_LEFT_ARM_ARMOR (30) -- PASS. (c) terminal combat state, lines 427-436, asserts terminalCustom.leftArmArmor <= CUSTOM_LEFT_ARM_ARMOR (30) (bounded, not strict equality, because damage may have reduced it -- correctly commented as such) -- this is a consistency check tied to the same session-unit id already proven correct at (a), not an independent substitution witness on its own, but it is not falsifiable by a canonical (34) unit either since 34 could also decay below 30. (d) the 'force record' point named in the review charter (GET /api/forces/:forceId, lines 322-329) asserts assignedUnitIds.toContain(customId) -- this is an IDENTITY check (unitRef), not an armor-VALUE check against 30; it does not appear anywhere in the preparer's own perStepAssertions as an armor assertion either (the preparer's own evidence correctly labels it a ref-identity check at 'step 8'). The roadmap.json launchProof.noSubstitution field's phrasing ('asserted at force record, in-session GameCreated seed, archived GameCreated snapshot..., terminal combat state') is imprecise: it implies 4 armor-value assertions where there are 3 value assertions plus 1 identity assertion. This does not weaken the overall no-substitution proof (the identity check at the force layer plus the roster-layer identity check at lines 276-281 close the identity-substitution gap that the armor checks alone would not), but the four-point description as literally written overstates what happens at the force-record hop.
findings.recommendation: Not a required edit to the spec (the spec's own comments and assertions are accurate); flagging only because the review charter's four-point framing, inherited from roadmap.json, should be corrected there if it is cited again.

findings.title: Product observation is accurate for persistMatchLog but imprecise for persistEncounterReplay
findings.detail: Read src/components/gameplay/pages/gameSession/GameSessionPage.lifecycle.ts in full. The receipt's claim ('Both effects fire on the completed-session transition and are not awaited; their cancelled flags suppress the callback but not the in-flight fetch. The guard that prevents re-fire is set in the resolve callback, so a re-render between fire and resolve issues a second identical POST') is precisely correct for persistMatchLog / POST /api/matches: the guard is React state `hasPersisted`, set via setHasPersisted(true) inside persistMatchLog's .then() callback (lines 130-149, consumed by the effect at lines 263-275 whose dependency array includes `session` and `hasPersisted`) -- i.e. genuinely set in the async resolve path, so a `session` reference change before that promise settles can re-run the effect and re-fire. It is NOT precisely correct for persistEncounterReplay / POST /api/replay-library/encounter: that effect's guard is a ref, `encounterPersistFiredRef.current`, set SYNCHRONOUSLY at line 288 -- inside the effect body, BEFORE the async call at line 289 -- not inside persistEncounterReplay's own .then() callback (lines 167-186 only guard the result-handling logic with a local `cancelled` flag, never touch the ref). Because the ref is a synchronous, same-tick latch, a plain 'session changed, effect re-ran' story does not by itself explain a second /api/replay-library/encounter POST the way it does for the state-gated /api/matches POST. The empirical duplicate observed in the preparer's own run-05.log is real (both endpoints double-fired in that run), but the receipt's single unified mechanism explanation only demonstrably holds for one of the two endpoints from the source as written; the replay-library duplicate's exact trigger (e.g. a remount reallocating a fresh ref, or some other path) is not fully explained by the cited lines.
findings.recommendation: Not required for this PR (task explicitly says do not fix); worth noting if the recommended follow-up PR is filed, so the follow-up's root-cause section does not inherit an unverified blanket explanation for both endpoints.

findings.title: Live run of the exact specified invocation FAILED due to shared-worktree build contamination, not a spec defect
findings.detail: Executed exactly: `MEKSTATION_E2E_SERVER_COMMAND='node .next/standalone/server.js' HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 MEKSTATION_E2E_PORT=3639 node scripts/playwright/run-playwright.mjs test e2e/saved-custom-combat-launch.spec.ts --project=chromium --retries=0 --workers=1` from the worktree root. Result: 1 failed, exit code 1. Failure: `Error: page.evaluate: Error: Campaign E2E stores are not exposed`, thrown from seedMissionOnCampaign (e2e/saved-custom-combat-launch.spec.ts:143-150) at test line 288. Root cause traced to source: src/lib/e2e/storeExposure.ts:31 `if (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE !== 'true') return;` short-circuits exposeStoresForE2E() before window.__ZUSTAND_STORES__ is ever assigned (line 34) whenever the client bundle was built without that flag set to the literal string 'true'. Corroborating evidence of build contamination: `.next/BUILD_ID` currently reads `1789484830850`, not the `1789483405493` the preparer's own evidence and the review charter both name; `.next/standalone/.next/BUILD_ID` matches the same newer `1789484830850`, mtime 2026-09-15 09:08:59 (this session), while `.next/standalone/server.js` itself carries an older mtime of 2026-09-15 05:06:27 -- internally inconsistent build state consistent with a second, later `npm run build` invocation (plausibly a vanilla/no-E2E-flags build, as another lane in this same session is documented doing at roadmap.json:2017-2027 in a sibling worktree) having overwritten this shared worktree's .next output after the preparer's original E2E-flagged build. The preparer's own build.log at `.sisyphus/roadmap-completion-20260912/r2-combat-browser-20260915/build.log` (cited in their evidence with a sha256) no longer exists on disk to cross-check. Per my charter I did not rebuild (the build was present, not missing) and did not modify any repo file. Nothing was left listening on port 3639 after the run (netstat showed only TIME_WAIT entries post-run); tsc and oxfmt were both run clean (see gates below).
findings.recommendation: REQUIRED ACTION (not a text edit): rebuild the standalone bundle for this worktree with `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE=true NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TEST=true npm run build` (matching the preparer's original command) in a moment when no other lane is writing to this shared worktree's .next output, then re-run the exact invocation above and confirm a green result before this proof is certified as verified-live. The spec file itself requires no changes.
